name: Zuiderkerk
description: The Zuiderkerk (Southern Church) on Zuiderkerkhof was the first church built in Amsterdam specifically for the Protestant community. Hendrick de Keyser designed it and it was built between 1603 and 1611 as a Renaissance hall church of brick with sandstone dressings. Its tower, about 80 metres tall, rises in square and octagonal stages with clock faces, corner columns and a lead-covered lantern; the clock bears the date 1614. The church closed for worship in 1929 and now houses an information centre for urban development and a venue.
funFact: The tower served as the model for De Keyser's later Westerkerk tower, and Rembrandt, who lived nearby on the Jodenbreestraat, had his children baptised here.
